Q1. Git/GitHub

No handwritten homework reports are accepted for this course. We work with Git and GitHub. Efficient and abundant use of Git, e.g., frequent and well-documented commits, is an important criterion for grading your homework.

  1. Apply for the Student Developer Pack at GitHub using your UCLA email. You’ll get GitHub Pro account for free (unlimited public and private repositories).

  2. Create a private repository biostat-203b-2026-winter and add Hua-Zhou and TA team (BowenZhang2001 for Lec 1; Tomoki-Okuno and yucais for Lec 82) as your collaborators with write permission.

  3. Top directories of the repository should be hw1, hw2, … Maintain two branches main and develop. The develop branch will be your main playground, the place where you develop solution (code) to homework problems and write up report. The main branch will be your presentation area. Submit your homework files (Quarto file qmd, html file converted by Quarto, all code and extra data sets to reproduce results) in the main branch.

  4. After each homework due date, course reader and instructor will check out your main branch for grading. Tag each of your homework submissions with tag names hw1, hw2, … Tagging time will be used as your submission time. That means if you tag your hw1 submission after deadline, penalty points will be deducted for late submission.

  5. After this course, you can make this repository public and use it to demonstrate your skill sets on job market.

Solution: The data files are distributed as .csv.gz files instead of .csv files to save storage space and reduce download times. Compressed files take up less disk space and can be transferred more quickly over the internet. This is particularly important for large datasets like MIMIC-IV, which can be several gigabytes in size. By using gzip compression, users can efficiently download and store the data without needing excessive storage capacity.

  1. Briefly describe what Bash commands zcat, zless, zmore, and zgrep do.

Solution: - zcat: This command uncompresses a list of files like .gz or its standard input and writes the uncompressed data on standard ouput. - zless: This command allows examination of compressed or plain text files one screenful on a terminal. If the files are compressed, the command uncompresses them itself. - zmore: This command also allows examination of compressed files and uncompresses them itself, one screenful at a time. - zgrep: This command searches expressions in compressed files, without needing to decompress them first.

Q4. Who’s popular in Pride and Prejudice

  1. You and your friend just have finished reading Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen. Among the four main characters in the book, Elizabeth, Jane, Lydia, and Darcy, your friend thinks that Darcy was the most mentioned. You, however, are certain it was Elizabeth. Obtain the full text of the novel from http://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/42671/pg42671.txt and save to your local folder.
wget -nc http://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/42671/pg42671.txt

Explain what wget -nc does. Do not put this text file pg42671.txt in Git. Complete the following loop to tabulate the number of times each of the four characters is mentioned using Linux commands.

wget -nc http://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/42671/pg42671.txt
for char in Elizabeth Jane Lydia Darcy
do
  echo $char:
  grep -woc $char pg42671.txt
done

Solution: wget -nc is a command that finds a file from the internet and downloads to the local directory, and with -nc flags, it makes sure that only one version is saved. The command will not work if the same file has already been downloaded. The grep command is used to search for the word with flags -woc to find the specific expression as a word and count the number of times it occurs. In Pride and Prejudice, Elizabeth is written more times than Darcy.

  1. What’s the difference between the following two commands?
echo 'hello, world' > test1.txt

and

echo 'hello, world' >> test2.txt
cat test1.txt
cat test2.txt
hello, world
hello, world

Solution: The first command uses >, which overwrites test1.txt and puts in the output of echo ‘hello, world’. The second command uses >> which appends the output of echo ‘hello, world’ to test2.txt.

  1. Using your favorite text editor (e.g., vi), type the following and save the file as middle.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Select lines from the middle of a file.
# Usage: bash middle.sh filename end_line num_lines
head -n "$2" "$1" | tail -n "$3"

Using chmod to make the file executable by the owner, and run

./middle.sh pg42671.txt 20 5

Explain the output. Explain the meaning of "$1", "$2", and "$3" in this shell script. Why do we need the first line of the shell script?

Solution: "$1", "$2", and "$3" are the arguments that follow after calling the shell script. "$1"is pg42671.txt, the file that contains Pride and Prejudice. "$2" is 20 and "$3" is 5. The shell script takes the first 20 lines of the text file and inputs it into the pipe to get the last 5 lines of the first 20. The lines 16, 17, 18, 19, and 20 are displayed from the text file. The first line of the shell script #!/bin/sh is a declaration that tells the operator which interpreter to use to execute the commands in the script.

Solution: - uname -a: displays the operating system implementation with -a flag allowing all details to be displayed - uptime: shows how long the system has been running, current ime, length of time system has been up, the numbers of users, and the load average of the system over the last 1, 5, and 15 minutes - who am i: displays information about the current logged in user, including login name, tty name, date and time of login, which is the current time - who: displays default information of the current logged in user - w: print a summary of the current activity of the system, including what the user is doing. - id: prints the users identity number, me and the guest user - last | head: shows the last logged in users, and head only shows the first 10 lines of the output

Q7. AI assistant

Which AI assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot) do you use when working on this assignment? Which AI model (e.g., GPT-5 mini, GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5) does the AI assistant use? How do you use them? Do you think they help improve your productivity?

Give 5 instances where AI model gave incorrect or misleading answers. You can use screenshots or copy-paste the Q&A.

Solution: I used two AI assistants working on this assignment. GitHub Copilot through RStudio and Claude Sonnet 4.5. GitHub Copilot helped me with writing bash scripts and commands, while Claude Sonnet 4.5 helped me with debugging my code when I received error messages. Both AI assistants helped improve my productivity by providing quick solutions and suggestions, allowing me to focus on understanding the concepts rather than getting stuck on specific coding issues.

Here are 5 instances where the AI model gave incorrect or misleading answers: 1. Copilot suggested an incorrect link for my Citi certificate. 2. Copilot suggested using an incorrect awk command to count unique patients. 3. Claude Sonnet 4.5 provided an incorrect solution for gzip decompression which caused additional errors. 4. Copilot suggested an incorrect description of my usage of Claude Sonnet 4.5.1.
